findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. User data is readable from the instance metadata service (including via SSRF against the internet-facing web server) and is stored unencrypted in Terraform state and visible in the AWS console, leaking long-lived credentials.

Ingress allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 on a security group attached to an instance in a public subnet with a public IP and an internet gateway route, exposing SSH to brute-force and exploitation from any source on the internet.
The egress rule permits all protocols to all destinations (0.0.0.0/0), giving a compromised host an unconstrained channel for data exfiltration and command-and-control.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data provisions only a plain Apache HTTP listener with no TLS, so all web traffic to this host traverses the internet in cleartext.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. On a publicly reachable web server whose user data contains AWS credentials, this makes credential theft via SSRF trivial.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root EBS volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest (including the user-data secrets persisted to disk) without cryptographic protection.

The instance is launched into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true and a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, attached to a security group open to the world, with no bastion, NAT, or load balancer boundary in front of it.
The EBS volume attached to the web host does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data written to the volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted EBS volume and therefore stores a persistent, unencrypted copy of the data that can be restored or shared by anyone with snapshot permissions.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry (internal addressing, traffic patterns) is stored without enforced encryption at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, restrictive ACL, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving protection against public exposure of network logs dependent on account-level defaults.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so flow log data may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the route table's 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, gives every instance launched here a public IP and direct internet reachability with no segmentation boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true exposes any instance launched into this subnet directly to the internet through the shared route table pointing at the internet gateway.
